reasons: Correctly identifies a Customer-side take-or-pay element: the parenthetical minimum monthly fees for Hosting and Support Services in p0045 are payable regardless of usage, which the playbook resists (preferred: pay for usage/ordered services only).

The redline reaches the preferred position directionally: the minimum-fee parenthetical is deleted and the consequential Section 6 carve-outs stripping documentation and dispute rights for those minimums are removed, restoring our audit/contest rights. Both edits favour Customer and introduce no new counterparty rights.

Comment is accurate (notes the amounts are currently blank), states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (floor limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, trued up rather than penalised) in the required tone.

The 0.723 changed-character ratio on p0045 is explained by the added confirming sentence ('Client will pay only for ... actually requested ... with no minimum purchase or minimum fee commitment'); the surrounding invoicing and other-services language is untouched. Strictly, deleting the parenthetical alone would suffice, so the extra sentence is optional belt-and-braces, but it is consistent with the rule and does not overreach.

Minor drafting nit for negotiation: the original Section 6 cross-refers to 'Section 4' minimums while the floor sits in Section 5(a); the finding notes the substance correctly and the deletion removes the stale cross-reference anyway.
